name: First-run tutorial / onboarding walkthrough
evidence: drove it: a phone with lk_onboarded and no lk_tutorialSeen lands on #/tutorial in the assembled demo; skip and finish both write lk_tutorialSeen and it survives a reload.

name: Notification / deep-link routing
gap: The routing is built and driven: ?open= and lk_openOnboarding pick a pane, a lockedPushOpen window event and a service-worker message route to a pane or to one of the three page crossings onboarding declares, and a target it cannot open says so rather than going somewhere else. What is missing is anything that would send such a notification — a push server, a VAPID key and a subscriptions table.
evidence: drove it

name: Resend confirmation
gap: The confirm pane exists, is reached from a sign-up that came back needing confirmation, and says what it is waiting on. The resend control needs a resend method on the one seam (Supabase /auth/v1/resend belongs in cloud.js, not in a second network call on this screen) and a server to answer it; with neither, it says nothing was sent.
evidence: drove it

name: Guest / anonymous mode
evidence: drove it: Continue as guest writes lk_guestMode=1, it survives a reload, and Settings opens in the guest state afterwards. The three no-server paths out of the account forms write the same key through the same helper.

name: Auth overlay UI
gap: Now carries the confirm mode and the paywall-adjacent copy it was missing, and every form goes through LKCloud rather than a timer. Still a full screen rather than an overlay over the app, which is deliberate: the flow is a takeover and the demo pushes it as one. Signing in needs window.LK_CLOUD.
evidence: drove it

name: Step 4 — AI coach chat interview (auto-kickoff)
gap: The interview screen is built and auto-kicks off: with a Worker configured the coach asks the first question without the person opening. With none it says so on the first frame and the chosen plan stands. Needs coachUrl and the Worker's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
evidence: drove it against a stubbed Worker

name: Step 4 — Answering questions (3-question loop, counter, send)
gap: Composer, send, Enter-to-send, a question counter and the three-answer loop are built and driven; the fourth send asks for the programme. Needs the Worker.
evidence: drove it against a stubbed Worker

name: Worker AI endpoint (`callWorker`) — the fetch at ~33857
gap: The call is LKCloud.ask, which is the one seam — no fetch, no headers and no token on this screen. Refuses with 'the coach needs a server' until coachUrl is set.
evidence: drove it against a stubbed Worker

name: Chat system prompt (`getChatSys`)
gap: getChatSys and getGenSys are written and sent with the call. They go in context.instructions because the Worker composes its own system message from context; a role:system turn would be dropped. Needs the Worker to have any effect.
evidence: read the contract in 15-server/coach-worker.js and drove the call

name: Program generation + parsing (`getGenSys`, `tryParseProg`)
gap: Generation and parsing are built: a split action from the Worker's structured reply, or a ###PROGRAM_START### block parsed as a fallback, both handed to LKCoachActions.check on the device, which resolves every id against the real catalogue and refuses the whole programme when one lift does not exist. Applying writes lk_splits and keeps the chosen plan. The local half now says in those words that the plan was chosen from a set of five and not built for them. Needs the Worker.
evidence: drove it: a good programme resolved to catalogue ids and saved; one with an invented lift was refused by name and wrote nothing

name: Program preview card (in-chat)
evidence: drove it: the card is drawn from the checked action, shows a row per split day with its exercises and the count recomputed here, and shows the refusal reasons instead when the check fails.

name: Shell chrome (status-bar scrim, toasts, voice button)
gap: The status-bar treatment, the toast and the shelf are in place and the voice button stays cut. A shared toast helper belongs in chrome.js so it cannot drift screen to screen, and chrome.js is not this package's file.
evidence: drove it

name: Supabase client bootstrap
gap: cloud.js is the Supabase bootstrap and both screens in this package now load it. It refuses every call with a printable reason until a deploy sets window.LK_CLOUD with the project URL and the publishable key.
evidence: drove it both ways: unconfigured refusals, and a configured client against a stubbed endpoint

name: Supabase `profiles` table read (App root)
gap: lk_profile is still the only profile this screen writes, and it syncs as a row in the store table like every other key. A read of the profiles table is not in the seam; if the username needs to be unique across accounts that is where it has to be checked, and it needs the table and a policy first.
evidence: read the schema

name: `getToken` / `headers` / `authHeaders`
gap: getToken and headers live in cloud.js and are used through it; nothing here reimplements them. They produce a real header once the anon key and a session exist.
evidence: read it and drove a signed-in call through it

name: Toast
gap: One helper and one slot on this screen, with a dismiss. The shared version belongs in chrome.js, which this package does not own.
evidence: drove it

name: Beta data sync (`/beta-sync`) — separate, legacy channel
gap: Cut with the rest of the beta subsystem, reason recorded in onboarding.html. A second sync channel beside LKCloud.sync would be two resolvers for one path; if beta data ever needs syncing it is a key in syncKeys() and the same store_push.
evidence: decided

name: The paywall sheet
gap: The sheet is built: price, the yearly alternative, the trial, what Pro adds, what stays free, and the tier this account is actually on. Pressing the trial button says checkout is not connected and nothing was charged, because there is no payment provider and nothing in the app can grant Pro.
evidence: drove it

name: Entitlement fetch & the `can()` gate
gap: The client half is over LKCloud.entitlement() and LKCloud.can(), with no second copy of the free list on this screen. It paints from the same cache the gate reads, so what it says and what it does cannot disagree. Needs entitlement rows and the webhook that writes them.
evidence: drove it with a stubbed entitlements endpoint

name: Actual runtime gating — server-side 429 / `gated`
gap: The client half is built: a 429 or a gated body from the coach call opens the paywall with the server's own reason instead of an error nobody can act on, and can('coach') is checked before anything is sent. The Worker does no gating yet — it has no entitlement check at all.
evidence: drove it: a stubbed 429 opened the sheet carrying the server's message

name: Trial banner
gap: The banner is built and counts the days from trial_ends. It is drawn from the entitlement and nothing else, so with no server it never appears and the Pro row states the price instead. Needs a real trialing row.
evidence: drove it with an entitlement of tier pro, status trialing, three days out

name: Silent beta
gap: Cut with the rest of the beta subsystem, reason recorded in onboarding.html: a silent-beta id list is an operator feature shipped to everybody, and the ids are readable by the client that carries them.
evidence: decided

name: Activity & AI logging
gap: Cut with the rest of the beta subsystem, reason recorded in onboarding.html: writing every question somebody asks the coach into a local key that then syncs is a privacy cost with no reader in this build. Anything worth seeing belongs in the server's own logs.
evidence: decided

name: Beta admin panel
gap: Cut, reason recorded in onboarding.html — an operator console inside a consumer app, which is the same ground the coach package cut its two beta-admin rows on.
evidence: decided

name: FOODS database
gap: Not a file this package owns. The fuel package has built the local food store (lk_myFoods holds both a table food at a weight you buy it in and a product with its own frozen figures and barcode), so the shape for anything looked up is there; widening the table itself and the USDA lookup are fuel.html, fixtures.js and the Worker key in 14-signoff/WORKER-USDA-KEY.md.
evidence: read the fuel store

name: PWA manifest and iOS install metadata
gap: Done on this package's two screens: an inlined manifest, the apple metas, theme-colour and the icon, matching what assemble.mjs puts in the assembled demo. The other sixteen standalone screens still have none and each one's owner has to add it, or it belongs in a shared head the build does not have.
evidence: drove it: the manifest link parses, names LOCKED, is display standalone and carries two icons

name: Install prompt (`beforeinstallprompt`)
evidence: drove it with a synthetic beforeinstallprompt: the control is hidden until the browser offers a prompt, calls prompt() once, and hides again afterwards.

name: Zoom lock
gap: Pinch is refused on this package's two screens; chrome.js already handles double-tap everywhere. The other sixteen screens still allow a pinch, and the three listeners belong in chrome.js, which this package does not own.
evidence: drove it: gesturestart is cancelled on both screens

name: Service worker → app messaging and push deep links
gap: The app side is built and driven: a service-worker message of type lockedPushOpen, and the window event of the same name, both go through one router that opens a pane or a declared crossing and says so when it cannot. The worker that would receive a push and post that message needs a push server, a VAPID key and a subscriptions table.
evidence: drove it

name: Boot self-heal for push subscriptions
gap: The boot check is built: with notifications granted and no push subscription, the overview says plainly that reminders are not set up and nothing will arrive. Resubscribing needs a VAPID key and a subscriptions table, so the screen reports rather than pretending to heal. Settings owns the notification controls and is not this package's file.
evidence: read it and drove the render path

name: Beta data collection and sync (touched by onboarding)
gap: Cut with the rest of the beta subsystem, reason recorded in onboarding.html.
evidence: decided
